scope: Targeted desktop integration previews; no surveyed paint/pole accuracy or worldwide acceptance.

samples.name: Berlin - marked signal approaches
samples.assessment: Candidate: road-control lines and visible signal indicators make the approach more legible. Nearby explicitly unmarked roads remain largely unpainted.
limits: Pole positions/counts and stop-line layout are inferred.
Some patterns and clipped fragments remain abrupt.

samples.name: London - Trafalgar Square streets
samples.assessment: Candidate: multiple lane dividers, crossing/control lines and indicators improve street structure.
limits: Underlying carriageway and island geometry remains approximate.
The simple signal cycle does not reconstruct actual turning conflicts or schedules.

samples.name: New York - Broadway marked street
samples.assessment: Candidate targeted street preview: lane paint, arrows, controls and indicators are visible from a road-centred start.
limits: Lane and arrow layouts are approximated from source attributes; some separately mapped line geometry has sharp transitions.
No claim of colour-calibrated or street-survey accuracy.

samples.name: New York - City Hall streets
samples.assessment: Limited: initial nearest-road snap centres on the paved Steve Flanders Square/plaza. Marked roads exist around the bake edges. Retained as evidence; Broadway is the road-focused preview.
limits: Road class alone does not establish public motor-vehicle access.
This result is not visually accepted as a road-marking showcase.
